results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Triceps Extension Pull
instructions: Stand with your back facing the ski ergometer machine, with the right foot a step forward and the other a step back for support. Hold the handles with both hands, palms facing each other, and upper arms parallel to the floor.
Begin by pulling both handles forward, extending your elbows, and engaging your triceps.
Continue pulling until your arms are fully extended in front of you, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows pointing forward to isolate the triceps.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Triceps Extension Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Pull Half Circles
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands.

Begin by pulling both handles downwards with your arms bent to 90 degrees until both elbows are close to your sides, while simultaneously lowering into a squat position, bending your knees and pushing your hips back.
Bring the handles back in a half-circle motion in a controlled manner as you stand back up from the squat.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Pull Half Circles is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Wide Lat Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles down in a wide arc motion while simultaneously lowering into a squat position, bending your knees, and pushing your hips back.
Continue pulling the handles down towards your sides until they are at hip level, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, and stand back up from the squat.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
Keep your upper body relaxed and avoid tensing your shoulders.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Squat Wide Lat Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Triceps Extension Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands, palms facing each other. Arms bent at 90 degrees with elbows pointing down.
Begin by pulling both handles down towards your hips, extending your elbows, and engaging your triceps.
Continue pulling until your arms are fully extended down, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your body to isolate the triceps.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Exhale as you extend your arms and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Triceps Extension Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Skipping
instructions: Stand with your feet together and arms by your sides as if holding the handles of a skipping rope, one in each hand. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Swing your hands in a circular motion as if turning a skipping rope, and jump lightly off the floor, keeping your knees slightly bent and landing softly on your forefeet.
Keep your jumps low and quick, simulating skipping with a rope. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on keeping your jumps low to the floor to minimize impact on your joints.
Stay relaxed and avoid tensing your shoulders and arms.
results.description: Skipping is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Shoulders.

results.name: Sled Battle Rope Pull
instructions: Attach a long rope to a loaded sled and walk away to the end of the rope.
Stand in an athletic stance, or sit, facing the sled.
Pull the rope hand over hand to bring the sled toward you.
Keep pulling until the sled reaches you.
tips: Keep your back flat and use your legs as an anchor.
Pull with your back, not just your arms.
results.description: Sled Battle Rope Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Sled Drag and Row
instructions: Attach a rope or straps to the sled and face it, holding the handles.
Walk backward a few steps, dragging the sled.
Stop, hinge slightly and row the sled toward you.
Alternate between walking backward and rowing.
tips: Keep your chest up when you walk backward.
Squeeze your shoulder blades on each row.
results.description: Sled Drag and Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Glutes, Lats.

results.name: Standing Toe Touch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Simultaneously lift your right leg straight up to hip height while raising your left arm to touch your right toes.
Return your right leg and left arm to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement on the opposite side. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping both your leg and arm straight throughout the movement.
Ensure your supporting leg remains slightly bent to maintain balance.
Keep your core tight to maintain balance and stability.
results.description: Standing Toe Touch is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Shoulders, Quadriceps.

results.name: Star Jump
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides, maintaining an upright posture.
Bend your knees slightly and lower into a half-squat position to prepare for the jump.
Explosively jump upwards, spreading your legs out to the sides and extending your arms overhead to form a star shape in mid-air.
Land softly with your feet together and your arms by your sides, immediately bending your knees to absorb the impact. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your leg muscles to generate the jump, avoiding excessive strain on your knees.
Ensure your knees are slightly bent as you land to absorb the impact and prevent injury.
Start with smaller jumps to perfect your form before increasing the height.
results.description: Star Jump is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Stationary Exercise Bike
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that when you sit on the bike, your feet can comfortably reach the pedals with a slight bend in your knees at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Sit on the bike with your back straight, and grip the handlebars lightly. Place your feet securely on the pedals, ensuring they are aligned properly.
Begin pedaling by pushing down on one pedal while pulling up on the opposite pedal, creating a smooth, circular motion.
Adjust the resistance level using the bike's control knob or digital settings to match your desired intensity. Continue pedaling for the duration of your workout.
tips: Maintain good posture by keeping your back straight and shoulders relaxed to avoid strain.
Start with a lower resistance level if you are a beginner and gradually increase it as you build strength and endurance.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling deeply and exhaling fully.
results.description: Stationary Exercise Bike is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes, Hip Flexors.
